fragments.text: Whatever time of day or wherever you are connecting from, I bring you very warm Caribbean greetings from the UNESCO Kingston office and my co-presenter, Miss Erica Simmons. I am Paul Hector, Advise of Communication and Information, and I'd like to express appreciation for the opportunity to share our work on the Caribbean AI Policy Roadmap. And, of course, special thanks to Mr. Cordell Green, EFAP, and all the amazing partners who are making this conference possible. Now, during my presentation, I will provide, next slide, during my presentation, I will provide an overview of UNESCO's work in the area of artificial intelligence. I will also highlight some Caribbean-specific initiatives, so as to set the stage for Erica's presentation, which will go into depth about the AI Policy Roadmap for the Caribbean.
fragments.summary: Whatever time of day or wherever you are connecting from, I bring you very warm Caribbean greetings from the UNESCO Kingston office and my co-presenter, Miss Erica Simmons.

fragments.text: Next slide. So what is UNESCO doing in the field of artificial intelligence? Well, interventions that are taking place across forming, supporting capacity building, sharing national regional and international experiences, and, of course, conducting research to support and inform evidence-based policy-making and decision-making. So, some examples of this work include the recommendations on the ethics of artificial intelligence, the world's first normative instrument of its kind, and two implementation tools, the RAM and the EIA. We also are running capacity building programs for a range of actors such as policymakers, judicial operators, civil servants, and, of course, journalists. We organize a variety of conferences and webinars, and also conduct research on the needs of women, developing countries with respect to artificial intelligence, and this is, of course, a very important input to supporting evidence-based policy-making, which is so essential for ensuring that no one is left behind.
fragments.summary: So what is UNESCO doing in the field of artificial intelligence?
